subsystems.name: Data ingestion
subsystems.role: pulls the company's financial and operational records into one canonical model.

subsystems.name: Regulatory knowledge base
subsystems.role: holds the law as machine-readable rules, versioned by jurisdiction and date.

subsystems.name: Control engine
subsystems.role: tests transactions and records against those rules before or as they are booked.

subsystems.name: Reporting and filing engine
subsystems.role: produces statutory returns and transmits them through government channels.

subsystems.name: Identity and screening
subsystems.role: checks counterparties against sanctions, politically exposed person and watch lists.

subsystems.name: Evidence and audit trail
subsystems.role: keeps an immutable record of what was filed, when and on what basis.

subsystems.name: Exception workflow
subsystems.role: routes anything the rules cannot resolve to a human.

buildSteps.title: Map the obligations
buildSteps.detail: Tax and legal specialists read each regulation and write down every duty, threshold, deadline and data field it requires.

buildSteps.title: Model the data
buildSteps.detail: Design a canonical schema for transactions, entities and periods so many source systems and many jurisdictions speak one language.

buildSteps.title: Build the connectors
buildSteps.detail: Write adapters for accounting systems, banks and payroll so records flow in without manual re-entry.

buildSteps.title: Encode the rules
buildSteps.detail: Turn each obligation into explicit, testable logic — rates, thresholds, rounding, effective dates — with automated tests against known cases.

buildSteps.title: Connect to authorities
buildSteps.detail: Integrate with government portals and APIs, using sandbox environments first, then live submission with signed receipts.

buildSteps.title: Run continuous monitoring
buildSteps.detail: Validation happens at the point of entry rather than at period end, so problems surface while they can still be corrected.

buildSteps.title: Record the evidence
buildSteps.detail: Log every check, decision and submission in a tamper-evident trail that stands up to an audit.

buildSteps.title: Maintain the rules
buildSteps.detail: A standing process watches for legal changes, updates the rule catalogue and re-tests before the effective date.

prerequisites.why: automation depends on authorities offering APIs and accepting structured submissions; coverage is very uneven between countries.
standard formats let invoices carry the data an authority needs without a human reading them.

prerequisites.tech: Cloud compute, storage and stream processing
prerequisites.why: real-time validation across millions of transactions requires elastic processing.

prerequisites.tech: Strong customer authentication and digital signatures
prerequisites.why: filings and approvals need legally binding proof of who submitted what.
law is written for humans; translating it into unambiguous logic is still largely manual and error-prone.

pathway.milestone: mandatory e-invoicing and real-time transaction reporting in several countries — Italy's SdI, Hungary's real-time invoice reporting, India's GST e-invoicing — plus AML transaction monitoring
pathway.unlocks: routine compliance without armies of staff, and tax authorities seeing transactions near-live.

pathway.milestone: pre-validation at the point of sale, where a transaction is checked and cleared as it is created
pathway.unlocks: fewer corrections and penalties; compliance becomes a design constraint rather than a clean-up job.

pathway.milestone: continuous audit and supervisory technology, with regulators querying company data directly rather than receiving annual returns
pathway.unlocks: assurance in near-real time, and earlier detection of systemic problems.

pathway.milestone: legislation drafted and published as machine-readable code alongside the human text
pathway.unlocks: shorter lag between a law passing and systems implementing it — though legal accountability stays with people.
